name: Send a weekly Google Search Console report to Slack with Claude observations checked by code

values.content:
=You write short observations about a website's Google Search Console numbers for this week. The numbered facts below were computed by code. Use ONLY these facts.

# Rules
- Write 3 to 5 observations, each one or two sentences, in {{ $("Config").first().json.output_language }}.
- Each observation lists the ids of the facts it uses in "fact_ids". Copy every number exactly as it appears in those facts (you may drop a minus sign and say "down" instead). Do not calculate new numbers (no sums, no ratios, no percentages that are not in the facts).
- When you name a query or a page, put it in quotes exactly as in the fact.
- Average position: lower is better. Do not call a higher position number an improvement. With few impressions (fewer than 100), one impression at a far position moves the average a lot: then do not present a change of the average position as a real trend.
- Queries are not shown for every impression (see the fact impressions_with_a_known_query): do not add up queries as if they were the whole.
- Do not guess causes as facts. If you mention a possible cause, say it is a possibility. If the numbers are small, say so.
- Output JSON only (no explanation, no code block): {"observations": [{"text": "...", "fact_ids": ["F1"]}]}

# Facts (JSON)
{{ JSON.stringify($json.facts) }}

nodes.name: Run once: set up the sheet

parameters.content:
## 1. Triggers and settings
Weekly on Monday, or on demand. Config holds the property, the period, the data lag and the language.

## 2. Ask Search Console
Six requests: totals, by query and by page, for this week and the week before.

## 3. Code computes the facts
Every number and change is computed here and numbered. An API error stops the run with a clear message instead of reporting zeros.

## 4. Claude writes, code checks
Claude may only use the facts. Code checks the numbers and quoted names of each observation and marks the ones that fail.

## 5. Save and post
One row per week in Google Sheets, and the report in Slack.

## Run once: set up the sheet
Paste your spreadsheet ID, run this branch once, and it adds the tab and the header row.

## Search Console weekly, with numbers you can trust
Every Monday the workflow pulls last week and the week before from the Google Search Console API. **Code computes every number** (clicks, impressions, CTR, average position, top / new / lost queries and pages) as a numbered list of facts. Claude writes 3–5 short observations from those facts only, and **code checks each one**: every number must be in the facts it cites, every quoted query or page must exist. The report goes to Slack and one row per week to Google Sheets.

### How it works
1. Six API calls (totals, by query, by page, for both weeks). Data is 3 days behind, so the week ends 3 days ago.
2. Code builds the facts, and says how many impressions have a known query (Search Console hides rare ones).
3. Claude writes observations with the fact ids it used. A failed check is shown with a warning, never hidden.

### Setup
1. In Google Cloud, enable the **Google Search Console API** in the project of your OAuth client.
2. Create a **Google OAuth2 API** credential with the scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/webmasters.readonly`.
3. Put your property in **Config** (`sc-domain:example.com` or `https://www.example.com/`).
4. Blank Google Sheet: paste its ID in **Spreadsheet ID**, run **Run once**, select the sheet. Pick a Slack channel.

### Customization
Change the language, the period, the minimum impressions and the list length in **Config**.
